### charley-forey/procore-mcp
- URL: https://github.com/charley-forey/procore-mcp
- Exact commit / revision: `855676f0c52171172b62c731c106f7ba69890612`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- What it contains: Very large Procore MCP/integration layer generated from an OpenAPI corpus: 2,755 typed tools, construction-financial/project-management/preconstruction domains, 70 capability bundles, 196 declarative workflows, personas/policies, router/evaluation tooling, multi-tenant transport, idempotency and audit/telemetry plumbing. Code search confirmed real construction-financial handlers/types for commitments, billing periods, schedule-of-values fields, change orders and prime contracts rather than README-only claims.
- Rare or undernoticed value: A nearly complete operational interface to the dominant construction system-of-record class. For ScopeSignal, the valuable part is the bridge from detected evidence to live RFI/financial/change-order/commitment records without hand-building thousands of endpoint wrappers.
- Likely buyer / user: GCs/EPCs and construction software vendors already using Procore.
- Painful problem: Evidence-first change detection is commercially weaker if a PM must manually re-key RFIs, commitments, budget/change-order and billing context into another product.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Procore-connected ScopeSignal diagnostic that reads project evidence/financial state, identifies human-reviewable leakage candidates, and writes nothing until an approved workflow is designed; later a paid integration tier.
- Build-time / data advantage: Potentially 4-8+ months of API typing, endpoint mapping, routing, policy and workflow integration discovery.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact latest commit; README architecture; `src/server/registry/registrations/construction-financials/commitments.ts`; `src/tools/construction-financials/commitments/definitions.ts`; construction-financial types including change orders/prime contracts; `package.json` build/eval/workflow-validation scripts and test commands.
- License / rights: `package.json` explicitly declares `license: "Private"` and no root LICENSE file was found. Public visibility is not a reuse grant. Procore API/platform terms also apply independently.
- Reuse classification: Inspect/learn/clean-room integration map only unless commercial permission/licensing is established.
- Why it is non-obvious: Repository naming suggests a normal MCP wrapper, but the actual surface includes generated endpoint coverage, construction workflows, policy gates and router evaluation at unusual depth.
- Score: A 4 / B 5 / C 5 / D 4 / E 5 / F 0 = **23/30**. Excellent integration evidence and commercial fit; rights block direct reuse.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal/Massing PDF/BIMChange/OpenTakeoff -> evidence candidate -> Procore clean-room connector -> RFI/change-event/commitment/change-order/billing context and approved downstream action.
- Next action: Independently map the minimum read-only Procore endpoints needed for one ScopeSignal pilot (RFIs, drawings/revisions, commitments, change events/orders, budget/SOV) and use official API documentation/terms for the production connector.

### Hotwodi/Construction-Profit-Guard-Job-Costing-Change-Orders-Billing-Intelligence
- URL: https://github.com/Hotwodi/Construction-Profit-Guard-Job-Costing-Change-Orders-Billing-Intelligence
- Exact commit / revision: `9cd740d810e3e31ef6cfd0dd08764c1ca0a7ece7`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- What it contains: Real Odoo 18 construction finance module with project contract value, budget baseline, actual/committed costs, change-order states/approval amounts, progress billing and subcontract commitments. Source computes approved-change totals, revised contract value, adjusted budget, billed/paid amounts and margin/profit.
- Rare or undernoticed value: Compact reference for turning an approved field/scope change into revised contract and margin state rather than stopping at a document alert.
- Likely buyer / user: Small/midsize contractors using Odoo or needing construction job-cost/change-order finance logic.
- Painful problem: Identifying a scope change does not create value unless it flows into contract value, budget, billing and margin protection.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Job-cost/change-order leakage diagnostic or a ScopeSignal finance adapter that quantifies accepted-change impact on contract value and gross margin.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 1-2 months of domain-model/workflow discovery for a construction finance bridge.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact commit/tree; `construction_profit_guard/models/cpg_project.py`; `cpg_change_order.py`; budget, cost-entry, billing and subcontract models; Odoo module manifest.
- License / rights: Module manifest declares LGPL-3, but a repository-root license grant was not found during inspection. Treat the declaration cautiously until applicability is confirmed.
- Reuse classification: Conditional/unclear; inspect and independently implement unless the LGPL grant is confirmed for the relevant files.
- Why it is non-obvious: Zero-attention Odoo module whose useful asset is the linkage between CO approval, revised contract, budget, billing and margin.
- Score: A 4 / B 4 / C 3 / D 3 / E 4 / F 2 = **20/30**.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal evidence -> human-approved CO -> Profit-Guard-style revised contract/budget/progress-billing/margin ledger.
- Next action: Recreate the minimal finance state machine independently and benchmark whether every approved/rejected CO produces auditable contract/budget/billing deltas.

### samsonovych/revitalize-permits-scraper
- URL: https://github.com/samsonovych/revitalize-permits-scraper
- Exact commit / revision: `e3874f1c9212851b0bb4ab7c38086cbc850d4054`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: MIT-licensed multi-jurisdiction permit ingestion framework with asynchronous list/detail scraper bases, Playwright support, typed Pydantic schemas, date-range chunking, atomic result persistence, region/city registries, jurisdiction-specific normalization/post-processing and an API/UI layer. The inspected tree contains implementations for Arlington, Austin, El Paso and San Antonio plus El Paso detail/post-processing tests and fixtures.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The README is empty, so the repository hides a much richer adapter architecture than its public presentation suggests. It addresses the expensive long tail of municipal permit portals and the normalization work required before permits become usable sales signals.
- Likely buyer / user: Permit intelligence vendors, contractor lead-generation products, building-material/HVAC/roofing/solar sales teams and real-estate/construction data companies.
- Painful problem: Municipal permits are fragmented across incompatible portals and schemas; national lead products fail when ingestion is brittle or city-specific normalization is hand-coded repeatedly.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Add one requested jurisdiction for a contractor/distributor and deliver a daily normalized permit feed; then roll the adapters into PermitPlate subscription coverage.
- Build-time / data advantage: Approximately 2-4 months of reusable scraper-base, region registry, browser automation, schema and post-processing design before adding more jurisdictions.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact latest commit/tree; MIT LICENSE; `permits_scraper/scrapers/base/permit_list.py` with validated date inputs, async execution, chunking and atomic persistence; city-specific large list/detail implementations; post-processing modules; `tests/test_el_paso_permit_details.py`, `tests/test_el_paso_post_processing.py` and fixtures.
- License / rights: MIT repository license verified. Rights/terms/robots/access rules of each municipal source remain separate and must be reviewed per jurisdiction; public permit fields can also include personal/contact data, which should be minimized and handled lawfully rather than indiscriminately retained.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT for repository code, subject to source-site/data terms and privacy minimization.
- Why it is non-obvious: Empty README and modest presentation conceal multiple real portal adapters, normalization modules and tests.
- Score: A 4 / B 4 / C 5 / D 4 / E 4 / F 5 = **26/30**. It is a strong build compressor, though coverage is still only a handful of jurisdictions and must be revalidated against live portals.
- Combination opportunities: `mzhc1/building-permit-scraper` completeness checks + this multi-city adapter framework + Urban Signal API feeds + PermitPlate property/entity resolution can form a resilient API-plus-portal national ingestion layer.
- Next action: Re-run the four adapters against their current lawful public endpoints, compare each collected interval to an independent portal/API count where available, and keep only jurisdictions that can prove completeness.

### Thatweirdguy1/industrial-management-cmms
- URL: https://github.com/Thatweirdguy1/industrial-management-cmms
- Exact commit / revision: `ccb2797b288df1be62cae1fa2b9e749dcd8d98da`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- What it contains: Full-stack industrial CMMS with QR machine lookup, breakdown reports with photo/document evidence, preventive work orders, risk scoring, spare-parts consumption forecasting, alerts, executive PDF reports and mobile-oriented technician workflows. Source search confirmed a real `predictive_engine.py` implementing recent-breakdown logic and inventory burn-rate processing.
- Rare or undernoticed value: Useful proof-of-work plus parts/asset-risk workflow in one system; stronger operational evidence than a generic ticket tracker.
- Likely buyer / user: Small industrial plants, maintenance contractors and facilities teams.
- Painful problem: Maintenance managers need evidence that work occurred, warning before repeat failures and enough parts on hand without overstocking.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price maintenance-operations diagnostic using QR work capture and proof-of-work, followed by managed reporting/PM scheduling.
- Build-time / data advantage: 2-3 months of CMMS workflow/UI/reporting/notification architecture.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact latest commit; README architecture and explicit rule descriptions; source search hit in `predictive_engine.py` for recent-breakdown and inventory burn-rate logic; deployment/config documentation.
- License / rights: README explicitly states PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 and prohibits commercial/production use without separate permission; no root LICENSE file was found. Do not use in a revenue product without permission.
- Reuse classification: Inspect/evaluate only for commercial purposes unless separate permission is obtained.
- Why it is non-obvious: The repo is framed as a portfolio-safe public version but contains a fairly complete plant-maintenance operating workflow.
- Score: A 4 / B 4 / C 4 / D 3 / E 4 / F 1 = **20/30**.
- Combination opportunities: Clean-room workflow ideas can strengthen JpAbg/CAFM + FM-DispatchBench: QR/proof-of-work and parts burn-rate signals -> optimized dispatch -> SLA/evidence packet.
- Next action: Do not copy code. Benchmark whether equivalent permissive components already in the facilities cluster can reproduce QR proof capture + parts-burn alerts.
